newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close off as strikes weaken bids.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close off as strikes weaken bids.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off in light trade for the fourth day running as investors stood back delaying bids until the dust of ongoing labor strife settled, traders said
The market's index slipped 0.53 percent to close at 6,295.02 points as 13 million shares traded worth 1.9 billion bolivars ($4 million).

"There was very little selling and little trade, although the index dropped," said Bancaracas broker Ricardo Larrazabal, adding that most investors were sitting on their hands while the labor conflict continued.

Some 40,000 teachers are in their second week of strikes following a nationwide doctors walk-out at the end of the year that was settled earlier this week by a government pay rise of up to 200 percent.
Among traded issues, 18 fell, 16 rose and nine closed flat.

Among widely-held shares, telephone company CANTV gained 11.25 bolivars to end at 1936.25, Electricidad de Caracas fell 3.00 bolivars to end at 482.00, while steel company Sivensa lost 1.00 bolivar to end at 314.00 bolivars.
